Benchmarking Screening Methods: Gene Set Scoring

Source: vignettes/Benchmark_GeneScore.Rmd
Benchmark_GeneScore.Rmd
library(SigBridgeR)
library(Seurat)

Overview

BenchGeneScore() scores one or more gene sets in every cell of a screened single-cell dataset. It does not compare labels against a ground truth like BenchAcc(); instead it asks whether the cells selected by different methods carry the pathway activity expected from the phenotype.

Four scoring backends are available:

method Backend Notes
"ssGSEA" GSVA::ssgseaParam() + GSVA::gsva() Rank-based, returns gene sets by cells
"AUCell" AUCell::AUCell_buildRankings() + AUCell::AUCell_calcAUC() AUC of the gene-set ranking
"UCell" UCell::ScoreSignatures_UCell() Fast rank-based scores, transposed to the common layout
"AddModuleScore" Seurat::AddModuleScore() Control-gene corrected mean expression

All backends return the same orientation: gene sets in rows and cells in columns. That makes it possible to switch backend or compare methods without reshaping the result.

A small example

The following object has twenty genes and eight cells. The first pathway is up-regulated in the "Positive" cells, while the second pathway is not, so the score matrix should separate the two groups for the first pathway.

truth <- rep(c("Positive", "Negative"), times = 4L)

counts <- Matrix::Matrix(
  matrix(
    rep(seq_len(20L), times = 8L) + rep(seq_len(8L), each = 20L),
    nrow = 20L,
    dimnames = list(paste0("Gene", seq_len(20L)), paste0("Cell", seq_len(8L)))
  ),
  sparse = TRUE
)

# * pathway A is active in the Positive cells
counts[1:5, truth == "Positive"] <- counts[1:5, truth == "Positive"] + 30L

sc <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)
sc <- NormalizeData(sc, verbose = FALSE)
sc$truth <- truth

pathways <- list(
  Pathway_A = paste0("Gene", 1:5),
  Pathway_B = paste0("Gene", 6:10)
)

BenchGeneScore() accepts a Seurat object, a ScreenMethodResult, or a BenchGeneScoreConfig. The pathway argument is a named list of gene sets:

scores <- BenchGeneScore(
  sc,
  pathway = pathways,
  method = "AddModuleScore",
  nbin = 4L,
  ctrl = 2L,
  verbose = FALSE
)

round(scores, 3)
#>            Cell1  Cell2  Cell3  Cell4  Cell5  Cell6  Cell7  Cell8
#> Pathway_A  0.734 -0.667  0.664 -0.533  0.607 -0.446  0.560 -0.384
#> Pathway_B -0.238  0.100 -0.211  0.077 -0.190  0.062 -0.173  0.053

The result is a gene-set-by-cell matrix whose columns match the cells of sc:

identical(colnames(scores), colnames(sc))
#> [1] TRUE

The group means show the expected pattern: Pathway_A is higher in "Positive" cells, while Pathway_B does not separate the groups.

round(
  apply(scores, 1L, function(x) tapply(x, sc$truth, mean)),
  3
)
#>          Pathway_A Pathway_B
#> Negative    -0.507     0.073
#> Positive     0.641    -0.203

Choosing a backend

The backend is selected with method. Additional named arguments in ... are matched against the formal arguments of the backend and, for two-stage backends, split over both stages automatically:

# * ssGSEA: extra arguments go to ssgseaParam() or gsva()
ssgsea_scores <- BenchGeneScore(
  sc,
  pathway = pathways,
  method = "ssGSEA",
  minSize = 5L,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# * AUCell: arguments are split between buildRankings() and calcAUC()
aucell_scores <- BenchGeneScore(
  sc,
  pathway = pathways,
  method = "AUCell",
  nCores = 1L,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# * UCell: arguments go to ScoreSignatures_UCell()
ucell_scores <- BenchGeneScore(
  sc,
  pathway = pathways,
  method = "UCell",
  maxRank = 500L,
  verbose = FALSE
)

The required package is loaded on demand with rlang::check_installed(), so the generic can be called even when only one backend is installed. In an interactive session, choose the backend that matches the question and keep it fixed when comparing screening methods:

  • "ssGSEA" and "UCell" are rank-based and robust to library-size and technical variation. They are a good default for comparing cell populations.
  • "AUCell" also uses rankings and is useful when the gene-set signal is concentrated in the top-expressed genes.
  • "AddModuleScore" is convenient when the object is already processed with Seurat, but it is sensitive to the choice of control genes and binning parameters (nbin, ctrl).

Configuration input

A BenchGeneScoreConfig runs the configured screening methods first and scores the accumulated labels in a single pass, so the scores are comparable across methods by construction:

config <- BenchGeneScoreConfig(
  matched_bulk = bulk,
  sc_data = sc,
  phenotype = phenotype,
  label_type = "{method_name}",
  phenotype_class = "binary",
  screen_method = c("Scissor", "scPAS"),
  method_param = MethodParamSet(
    Scissor_param = list(alpha = 0.05),
    scPAS_param = list(alpha = 0.01)
  ),
  bench_config = BenchGeneScoreConfigSet(
    method = "ssGSEA",
    minSize = 5L
  )
)

scores <- BenchGeneScore(config, verbose = FALSE)

BenchGeneScoreConfigSet() stores the backend and its arguments; the scoring backend’s package is checked when the configuration is built, so a missing dependency is reported before the screening run starts.

Reading the scores

A gene-set-by-cell matrix is deliberately simple: each value is a relative activity score for one gene set in one cell. It is not a p-value and should not be compared across datasets or across different backends as if it were on a common absolute scale.

Useful summaries are:

# * mean score per ground-truth or cluster label
cluster_mean <- apply(
  scores,
  1L,
  function(x) tapply(x, sc$truth, mean)
)
round(cluster_mean, 3)
#>          Pathway_A Pathway_B
#> Negative    -0.507     0.073
#> Positive     0.641    -0.203

# * rank cells within each gene set
pathway_rank <- t(apply(scores, 1L, rank))
pathway_rank[, 1:4]
#>           Cell1 Cell2 Cell3 Cell4
#> Pathway_A     8     1     7     2
#> Pathway_B     1     8     2     7

A common workflow is to compare the distribution of a pathway score across the cells selected by two methods. Because the matrix shares its columns with the Seurat object, the labels can be attached directly:

sc$Pathway_A <- scores["Pathway_A", ]

aggregate(
  Pathway_A ~ truth,
  data = sc[[]],
  FUN = mean
)
#>      truth  Pathway_A
#> 1 Negative -0.5074308
#> 2 Positive  0.6413492

Practical notes

  • Keep the backend fixed. ssGSEA, AUCell, UCell and AddModuleScore use different scales. Comparing methods is meaningful only when every method is scored by the same backend with the same arguments.
  • Match the identifier space. Pathway genes must match the row names of the assay. Convert symbols/Ensembl IDs or select the matching assay and layer first.
  • Missing genes are handled differently. AddModuleScore drops genes and gene sets that are absent from the assay; other backends may return NA or silently score fewer genes. Inspect the result whenever a pathway disappears.
  • The Seurat metadata is left untouched. AddModuleScore is called with an internal column prefix, so the score matrix is returned without adding columns to sc.
  • Scores are relative. High activity means “high within this dataset and this backend”, not “biologically active above a universal threshold”. Use group comparisons and ranks rather than absolute cut-offs.

See also

  • BenchGeneScoreConfig() and BenchGeneScoreConfigSet() for the configuration interface.
  • BenchGSEA() for pathway enrichment of method marker genes.
  • BenchAcc() for classification accuracy against a ground truth.
  • BenchMemory() for run time and memory.
